Title: Creating Shoes
Content: Objective Create shoes content by using CLO software. (The 'Register Accessory' function, which registers accessory files (*.zacs), is only available in CLO and is not supported in Marvelous Designer.) 1. How to Create Shoes to be registered as Accessory (ZACS) 1-1. Create shoe modeling in other 3D software. 1-2. Create shoes with the patterns in CLO. 1-1. Create Shoe Modeling in other 3D software. Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling shoes. Required &amp Recommended [Required] The accessory file must be created in FBX / COLLADA format to be registered as the ZACS. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. The file should not include anything other than Shoe meshes. (e.g. select Shoe Meshes only when exporting) Please specify the compatible avatars for the ZACS in the Description. The name of the Shoes Mesh must be "Shoes_L" or "Shoes_R," case-insensitive. For the heels, The heel part should be applied with a separate material, and the material should be applied last. [Recommended] The scanned data is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. It is strongly recommended to create shoe models using a maximum of 200,000 triangles, and please make sure that the polygon count does not go over 200,000. If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. Textures recommends using a maximum of 2048 pixels. Create a thumbnail image that shows the item well, which is recommended to be 400*300 pixels. To avoid abnormal collisions between garments and shoes during simulation, creating a transparent Dummy Mesh that covers the entire shoe is recommended. (Please refer to the Dummy Mesh Guide) Modifying content provided by other platforms may violate copyrights and result in the removal of the item. Before proceeding with shoe production, you must prepare the avatar file for generating accessories (ZACS). If you already prepared an avatar to utilize for accessories (ZACS), you can skip this step. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. Export the avatar as OBJ / FBX / GLTF or any format suitable for your 3D program. 4. Import the avatar file saved in step #3 into your 3D program and create Shoe Modelings. 5. Save the created shoe modeling as FBX / COLLADA. 1-2. Create Shoes with the patterns in CLO. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. Create shoes with the patterns in CLO. 2. Registering ZACS Register either shoe modelings created in other 3D programs or shoes with patterns as the ZACS. 1. Run CLO 2. Import the Avatar File into CLO. From the main menu, File &gt Open &gt Avatar &gt Register ACCESSORY &gt Select the Avatar file (AVT) that you want to utilize for ACCESSORY. 3. From the main menu, Avatar &gt Register Accessory Basic Accessory Type : Shoes Select Flats / Heels Object [File/Pattern] File Click the Folder icon to load the 3D file to be registered as Accessory. Scale : Adjust the scale of the shoes. Axis Conversion : Adjust the axis of the shoes. Pattern Select the patterns that you wish to register as Accessory (ZACS). However, the pattern to be converted must be created in advance before registering as an accessory. Note: After selecting the patterns to be converted into an accessory, you can register them as an accessory by right-clicking on the pattern in the 3D window, and then selecting Convert &gt to Avatar Accessory. Option Mirror Creation : The other side of the shoes will be generated on the opposite foot based on the center axis of the avatar. Thumbnail [Auto/Custom] : Register the Thumbnail image for the ZACS to be created. When 'Auto' is selected, the Thumbnail image will be generated automatically When 'Custom' is selected, click the '+' button to select the Thumbnail image you want to register. Save After choosing the save path for the ZACS, click the Save (S) button to generate the ZACS. 3. Modifying the material of ZACS You can modify the textures and materials applied to the generated ZACS in Property Editor. Click on the ZACS file in the 3D Window. 2. Apply textures and materials in the Property Editor. 1. Click on the ZACS in the 3D window. 2. Apply textures and materials in the Property Editor. 4. Saving the ZACS Save the Shoes ZACS file with all textures and materials applied. 1. from the main menu, File &gt Save As &gt Accessory 2. After specifying the file name and directory path, click Save (S). 3. Save Accessory Select Accessory : Select the type of Accessories (ZACS) Use Custom Image : Register Thumbnail image. Note: If you want to utilize the Thumbnail image that was created when registering the ZACS as is, you can leave it unchecked. 4. Click 'OK.' 5. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description When uploading the ZACS to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers. If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process. 1. UPLOAD (Mandatory) Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the REUPLOAD button if necessary. 2. TITLE (Mandatory) Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. 3. DESCRIPTION please specify the Avatar file (AVT) that is compatible with ZACS in the Description. (e.g. Available on FV2 avatars, but best suited to FV2_Yuna) 4. TAGS 'TAGS' is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. 5. ATTACHMENT You can attach files relating to the ZACS. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to 'ATTACHMENT' are being used. 6. ADD SUB-IMAGES You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the ZACS. 7. THUMBNAIL Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the ZACS. If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please register the rendered image. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.
ContentDescription: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide on creating and registering shoe models as accessories (ZACS) using CLO software, including detailed requirements, processes, and best practices for optimal results.

Title: Creating Button
Content: Objective Create Button items by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Required &amp Recommended [Required] The meshs normal direction should be facing outwards. The point where the OBJ button will be anchored to the garment must be placed at the origin (0,0,0). In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Recommended] Button OBJs should be made with less than 10,000 triangles, so there is no speed problem in CLO software simulation. UVs should be unwrapped to prevent overlapping, enabling users to apply a variety of textures without issues. In the case of a button with a thread, the thread mesh must be named 'Ren_Thread' to separate the button and thread from the CLO software Material. (To create BTN file by THREAD TYPE for reference) If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. please use the Normal map for the complex graphic pattern. (e.g. logo, pattern, etc.) It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 512 pixels. The scanned data is compatible, but the mesh should be meshed and editable. It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. 1. Checking the Direction and Position of the Button OBJ Please import the button OBJ into CLO to make sure that the position and direction of the Button OBJ are correctly set, before registering the button. Mesh Image with the correct position and orientation Mesh Image with the wrong position and orientation 2. Converting BTN format in CLO software: Only CLO-formatted files can be uploaded to CONNECT. All buttons must be saved in BTN format in CLO software. To save in BTN format, you need to have OBJ files. If you have a different format other than OBJ, export it as an OBJ format file from other 3D MODELING software. 2-1. Open CLO 2-2. Move to the Button Tab and select the button tab from the Object Browser. 2-3. To register BUTTON, click the register button next to the Shape menu in PROPERTY EDITOR. 2-4. Enter registration information 1. Name: Enter the name of the BTN to be sold. 2. If the OBJ files differ for each button size, click the '+' button beside tab '1' to register buttons of various sizes. 3. OBJ: Load the OBJ to be registered as a button. Select Mesh: Check the mesh corresponding to buttons and threads in the OBJ file. The selected Mesh will be highlighted in yellow in the Preview window. 4. Specification Width(mm): Width of the button Thickness(mm): Thickness of the button Weight(g): Weight of the button 5. Set as Default: Set as the default size for the BTN. 'Set as Default' is always checked when creating a single button. Make sure to check it in the file that you intend to set as the default size if you are creating multiple sizes. 6. Axis Conversion: adjust the axis of the OBJ in real-time. 7. Preview: Preview the imported OBJ button. 8. Click the OK button 3. Modifying the material of the BUTTON 2-1. Modify the Button's properties: You may adjust the material and properties of BTN in the Property Editor. Name. Modify the name of the button as needed. Shape. Adjust the size, thickness, and weight of the BUTTON. modifications are possible if the specification is 'Custom.' On the other hand, for the Size Button, modifications are not allowed. Material. Select the BUTTON's material, Color, and Texture from the Type Option. 3-2. Click the SAVE button in the PROPERTY EDITOR, to save it in BTN format. 4. creating THREAD TYPE BTN CLO SOFTWARE provides functionality that allows you to edit the visible THREAD when securing BUTTON. CROSS, PARALLEL, and SQUARE are three THREAD TYPES that can be created. To utilize the Thread Type feature, it is essential to have all three types of *.BTN files: Cross, Parallel, and Square. For button files utilizing the Thread Type feature, add '_Cross,' '_Parallel,' and '_Square' to the file name after OBJ. This naming convention applies only to the Button OBJ files using the Thread Type feature. 4-2. Generate the OBJ files for THREAD TYPE in step 4-1. - Make sure that the names of OBJ files for each THREAD TYPE are set as *_Cross.obj, *_Parallel.obj , *_Square.obj. 4-3. Create BTN files from previously generated OBJ files. 4-4. Save the generated *_Cross.btn, *_Parallel.btn, and *_Square.btn files to the following path: C:UsersPublicDocumentsCLOAssetsMaterialsHardware_and_TrimsButton &amp ButtonholeButton. 4-5. Run CLO and adjust the Button's Thread Type in the Property Editor under Shape&gt Thread Type. 5. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description When uploading the BTN to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers. If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process. 1. UPLOAD (Mandatory) Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the REUPLOAD button if necessary. 2. TITLE (Mandatory) Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. 3. DESCRIPTION If you are selling a physical product, please provide the sales page URL in the description. Please provide the default size of the BUTTON that you created for customers. Please provide the button units or the BTN information referencing the Property Editor in CLO / Marvelous Designer. X(mm) Y(mm) Z(mm) weight(g) 4. TAGS 'TAGS' is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. 5. ATTACHMENT You can attach files relating to the BTN. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to 'ATTACHMENT' are being used. 6. ADD SUB-IMAGES You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the BTN. 7. THUMBNAIL Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the BTN. If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please register the rendered image. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.
ContentDescription: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for creating and registering button items in CLO and Marvelous Designer, detailing essential requirements, recommended practices, and the step-by-step process for successful asset preparation and upload.

Title: Payout method
Content: Payment through PayPal Revenue will be paid through the PayPal account you entered when filling out the Seller Info. Additional Guidance If there are issues with your PayPal account, payments will be temporarily suspended, and you will receive a request to resubmit Seller Info. If you wish to change the PayPal account receiving the revenue, you must resubmit Seller Info. If the newly submitted Seller Info is not approved before the payment date, the payment may be deferred to the next month. Payment through Bank Transfer For sellers who cannot use PayPal, payment through wire transfer will be processed twice a year. Payments are made in June and December. How to Receive Payment via Wire Transfer 1. Provide the following information to the administrator through the Connect inquiry: CONNECT Name CONNECT (CLO-SET) account Name (real name) Swift code IBAN (International Bank Account Number) Country (with bank account) 2. Submit Seller Info. When submitting Seller Info, enter the PayPal account as follows: (ex- withoutpaypal@clo-set.com ) Additional Guidance Payment through bank transfer is only possible for countries that cannot use PayPal or under special circumstances. Even if you have provided bank account information, if Seller Info is submitted and fails the inspection, earnings will not be paid. If both steps 1 and 2 are completed, earnings will be transferred to the registered account in June and December. You may receive an email confirming the completion of PayPal payment, but it has been transferred to the bank account, so you may disregard it. If you want to change the bank account information, you must resend the information for step 1 before the payment is delivered.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides essential information on receiving payments through PayPal or bank transfer, including guidelines for submitting Seller Info and handling account changes.

Title: Digital Stamp
Content: 1. Get ready with your digital crypto wallet Connect your digital wallet to your Collection page. Once you connect your digital wallet, this wallet address will be linked to your CLO-SET CONNECT account. CLO web3 service supports a crypto wallet provided by MetaMask, Coinbase, etc. In case you don't have a digital wallet, you can make a new one. *Disconnecting or changing your digital wallet to your CLO-SET CONNECT account is not available for now. 2. Get Digital Stamp on your 3D design Go to the detail page of the item for which you want to receive a Digital Stamp. You can get a Digital Stamp on your Store and Gallery items. Click the "Digital Stamp" button at the bottom of the item detail page. Once you click the button, the metadata of the item is successfully stored on the blockchain, and the Digital Stamp is issued. *Normally, this process takes 10 seconds, but it can take up to 2 minutes depending on the situation of the blockchain network. If it takes longer than that, please try again or contact us. 3. Check your Digital Stamp On the creator Collection page, you will have a Digital Stamp tab and can check the item empowered by NFT technology. You can check the detailed information written on the blockchain in the detail section of your Digital Stamp. You will be able to import the Digital Stamp (NFTs) and see the item on your digital wallet as well. 4. Update your Digital Stamp In case you edit your item information after you got Digital Stamp - such as thumbnail, description, item attributes, etc. Go to the detail page of the item you want to update. If the item has been updated, the "UPDATE Digital Stamp" button is enabled, and if there is no update, the button is disabled. Click the "UPDATE Digital Stamp" button to proceed with the update of the blockchain data, which is metadata. At this point, the updated metadata of the item is successfully stored on the blockchain, and this result is updated to the current Digital Stamp.
ContentDescription: "Connect your digital wallet to CLO-SET CONNECT to effortlessly receive, check, and update Digital Stamps for your 3D designs, ensuring secure blockchain storage and easy access to NFT technology."

Title: Creating Motion (MTN) - Auto Conversion
Content: Objective Create a Motion file (.mtn) using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Converting and redistributing motions downloaded for free or purchased from other platforms is prohibited to protect the original creators' rights. Please create and use a motion file (.mtn) for personal use only. Examples: Mixamo, DAZ 3D, Reallusion-Actorcore, Unreal Marketplace, Artstation Marketplace, Sketchfab, etc 1. How to Create a motion file (.mtn) via auto-convert features Manual - Auto Convert to Avatar (CLO/ Marvelous Designer) Manual - Auto Convert to Motion (CLO) Note: 'Auto Convert to Motion' is currently compatible with Mixamo only. 1-1. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with the CLO avatar. 1-2. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with a custom avatar. 1-1. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with the CLO Avatar When using the CLO avatar, you can skip the 'Auto Convert to Avatar' and move directly to 'Auto Convert to Motion.' Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. From the main menu, click on File &gt Open &gt Avatar, or click on Avatar in the Library. Load your desired CLO Avatar. From the main menu, click on Avatar &gtAuto Convert to Motion Select the gender and the motion file (.fbx) you have created or downloaded. Click 'Convert' when ready. Save the motion file (.mtn) by clicking 'Save' when the auto-conversion is finished. Note: If you changed the CLO avatar's body shape, please save the avatar size file (.avs) in advance so you can easily match the size of the dummy CLO avatar displayed during 'Auto Convert to Motion' to your avatar. 1-2. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with a Custom Avatar When using a custom avatar, you must run the "Auto Convert to Avatar" before applying any motion files (.mtn). Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. From the main menu, click on Avatar &gt Auto Convert to Avatar Set the options and adjust the dummy CLO avatar's body shape using Avatar Editor while the 'Auto Convert to Avatar' is on. (Click the LINK to check the tutorial.) From the main menu, click on Avatar &gtAuto Convert to Motion Select the gender and the motion file (.fbx) you have created or downloaded. Click 'Convert' when ready. Save the motion file (.mtn) by clicking 'Save' when the auto-conversion is finished. Note: Please adjust the dummy CLO avatar displayed during 'Auto Convert to Motion' using the Avatar Editor to match your custom avatar's body shape. 2. Create a Thumbnail Image You can upload a thumbnail for the motion file in an image or an animation. If you are creating the thumbnail as an animation, please use approximately 100 to 200 frames from the entire motion sequence for the thumbnail. Tip: you can make the motion thumbnail longer as long as GIF/WebP animations don't exceed 50 megapixels (the sum of sizes of all frames). Please refer to the following website. Activate 'Quality Render (3D window).' Check 'Show 3D Shadow' under Environment Display. Check off 'Show Ground Grid' under Environment Display. Right-click on the 3D window, go to Format 3D background &gt Solid Color, and set the background color to #1A1A1F. Change the mode to 'Animation' at the top-right corner. From the main menu, File &gt Video Capture &gt Record Animation. Set the Orientation to 'Portrait' and the resolution to 750 x 1000 pixels. Start recording the animation. Convert the animation sequence (.mp4) to webp format. webp conversion website (Link #1, Link #2) 3. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description When uploading the motion file (.mtn) to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers. If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process. 1. UPLOAD (Mandatory) Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the REUPLOAD button if necessary. 2. TITLE (Mandatory) Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. 3. DESCRIPTION please provide the duration of the motion file (.mtn) and specify the Avatar file (AVT) that is compatible with the motion file (.mtn) in the Description. ( When uploading a file, if you have selected "Others" under SET AVATAR CATEGORIES &gt Compatibility, please provide the name and link of the avatar file (.avt) that is compatible with the motion file (.mtn). ) 4. TAGS 'TAGS' is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. 5. ATTACHMENT You can attach files relating to the motion file (.mtn). However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to 'ATTACHMENT' are being used. 6. ADD SUB-IMAGES You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the motion file (.mtn). 7. THUMBNAIL Register a motion thumbnail that showcases the motion file's characteristics (.mtn). If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please add the rendered sub-images. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on creating Motion files (.mtn) using CLO and Marvelous Designer software, while emphasizing the importance of respecting creators' rights by using these files for personal use only.

Title: Creating Pose/Motion (2024.2)-CLO Avatar
Content: Objective Creating a Pose or Motion file (.pos or .mtn) using 'Register Pose/Motion' in CLO or Marvelous Designer 2024.2. Note: Converting and redistributing motions downloaded for free or purchased from other platforms is prohibited to protect the original creators' rights. Please create and use a motion file (.mtn) for personal use only. Examples: Mixamo, DAZ 3D, Reallusion-Actorcore, Unreal Marketplace, Artstation Marketplace, Sketchfab, etc Essential Rules The following conditions must be met to properly register a pose or motion: 1. Download the CLO or Marvelous Designer Avatar Templates (aka. CLO Avatar) below to create pose or motion files for CLO or Marvelous Designer. CLO or Marvelous Designer Avatar Templates Adults Kids Babies 2. The animated CLO avatar must have the same joint factors listed below to be compatible with the CLO avatar template: Skeletal Structure Total number of the joints Joint Names Joint Axis Orientation The scale value of the 'Root' joint must be kept at 1.0. 3. The animated CLO avatar must maintain the same Bind Pose* as the CLO template file. *Bind Pose: The initial position of your character when the joints are skinned to the mesh. 4. 3D Program Preferences Unit Scale: Centimeter (cm) Animation Frame Rate: 30 FPS 5. Bake Keyframes must bake the animation to keyframes for all joints at every frame. 6. When posing or animating in Blender, make sure to reference 'Creating Pose/Motion (2024.2)-Tips for Blender.' 1. How to Create a pose file (.pos) Note: If the generated pose file is not properly applied to the avatar, please check again to make sure that all the essential rules above have been followed. 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer 2024.2. 2. From the main menu, click on Avatar &gt Register Pose/Motion. 3. In the 'Register Pose/Motion' Window, select the type 'Pose' and import your posed CLO avatar file (.fbx) by clicking the folder icon. 4. Once the file is loaded, CLO or Marvelous Designer will automatically identify the avatar and categorize it as either adult or child. If the avatar is an adult, please select either Male or Female in the Gender option based on the avatar's gender. 5. Please select the 'Shoe Type' and save the pose file (.pos) to your preferred location by clicking the 'Save' button. Shoe Type: Specify the shape of the feet for the avatar animation you created. 'Shoe Type' Setting For Males and Kids, the 'Shoe Type' is automatically set to Flats, and only displays the Gender option as shown in the image below. For Females, you can select between 'Heels' and 'Flats.' 6. Please apply the generated pose file (.pos) to your CLO avatar to see if it works correctly. 2. How to Create a motion file (.mtn) Note: If the generated motion file is not properly applied to the avatar, please check again to make sure that all the essential rules above have been followed. 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer 2024.2. 2. From the main menu, click on Avatar &gt Register Pose/Motion. 3. In the 'Register Pose/Motion' Window, select the type 'Motion' and import your animated CLO avatar file (.fbx) by clicking the folder icon. 4. Once the file is loaded, CLO or Marvelous Designer will automatically identify the avatar and categorize it as either adult or child. If the avatar is an adult, please select either Male or Female in the Gender option based on the avatar's gender. 5. Please select the 'Shoe Type' and 'Region' options that suit your preferences. Shoe Type: Specify the shape of the feet for the avatar animation you created. 'Shoe Type' Setting For Males and Kids, the 'Shoe Type' is automatically set to Flats, and only displays the Gender and Region option as shown in the image below. For Females, you can select between 'Heels' and 'Flats.' Region: Select the range of the animation to save. Entire: Save the entire animation range. Play Only: Save the animation range from the specified start frame to the end frame. Current Frame: Save the current frame of the animation. 6. Please click the 'Save' button to save the motion file (.mtn) to your preferred location. 7. Please apply the generated motion file (.mtn) to your CLO avatar to see if it works correctly. 3. Creating a thumbnail image for the uploaded motion file. You can upload a thumbnail for the motion file in an image or an animation. If you are creating the thumbnail as an animation, please use approximately 100 to 200 frames from the entire motion sequence for the thumbnail. Tip: you can make the motion thumbnail longer as long as GIF/WebP animations don't exceed 50 megapixels (the sum of sizes of all frames). Please refer to the following website. Activate 'Quality Render (3D window).' Check 'Show 3D Shadow' under Environment Display. Check off 'Show Ground Grid' under Environment Display. Right-click on the 3D window, go to Format 3D background &gt Solid Color, and set the background color to #1A1A1F. Change the mode to 'Animation' at the top-right corner. From the main menu, File &gt Video Capture &gt Record Animation. Set the Orientation to 'Portrait' and the resolution to 750 x 1000 pixels. Start recording the animation. Convert the animation sequence (.mp4) to WebP format. TIP: You may be able to find many websites for converting to WebP on the internet. 4. CONNECT Upload - Entering Asset Description When uploading the pose or motion file (.pos or .mtn) to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers. If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process. 1. UPLOAD (Mandatory) Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the REUPLOAD button if necessary. 2. TITLE (Mandatory) Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. 3. DESCRIPTION please specify the Avatar file (.avt) that is compatible with the pose or motion file (.pos or .mtn) in the Description. Title: Creating Earring
Content: Objective Create ZACS content by using CLO. (The 'Register Accessory' function, which registers accessory files (*.zacs), is only available in CLO and is not supported in Marvelous Designer.) 1. How to Create an Earring to be registered as Accessory (ZACS) 1-1. Create an Earring in other 3D software. 1-2. Create an Earring with the patterns in CLO. 1-1. Create an Earring in other 3D software. Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling Earrings. Required &amp Recommended [Required] The accessory file must be created in FBX / OBJ / COLLADA format to be registered as the ZACS. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. The file should not include anything other than an Earring mesh. (e.g. select an Earring Mesh only when exporting) Please specify the compatible avatars for the ZACS in the Description. [Recommended] It is strongly recommended to create an Earring mesh using a maximum of 50,000 triangles, and please make sure that the polygon count does not go over 50,000. If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. It is recommended to use textures using a maximum of 2048 pixels. Create a Thumbnail image that shows the item well, which is recommended to be 400*300 pixels. Modifying content provided by other platforms may violate copyrights and result in the removal of the item. Before proceeding with the Earring production, you must prepare the avatar file for generating accessories (ZACS). If you already prepared an avatar to utilize for accessories (ZACS), you can skip this step. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. Export the avatar as OBJ / FBX / GLTF or any format suitable for your 3D program. 4. Import the avatar file saved in step #3 into your 3D program and create an Earring Mesh. 5. Save the created Earring Mesh as FBX / OBJ / COLLADA. 1-2. Create an Earring with the patterns in CLO. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. Option Thumbnail [Auto/Custom] : Register the Thumbnail image for the ZACS to be created. When 'Auto' is selected, the Thumbnail image will be generated automatically. After specifying the file name and directory path, click Save (S). 3. Save Accessory Select Accessory : Select the type of Accessories (ZACS) Use Custom Image : Register Thumbnail image. Note: If you want to utilize the Thumbnail image that was created when registering the ZACS as is, you can leave it unchecked. 4. Click 'OK.' 5. UPLOAD (Mandatory) Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the REUPLOAD button if necessary. 2. TITLE (Mandatory) Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. 3. DESCRIPTION please specify the Avatar file (AVT) that is compatible with ZACS in the Description. (e.g. Available on FV2 avatars, but best suited to FV2_Yuna) 4. TAGS 'TAGS' is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. 5. ATTACHMENT You can attach files relating to the ZACS. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to 'ATTACHMENT' are being used. 6. Title: Tips & best practices
Content: You can reset CLO/MD LiveSync Editor by closing the active instance of the Editor, then reopening it. Due to how CLO and Marvelous Designer behave, they can be unresponsive when it is processing a big amount of data. Such situation is as the following: Right after hitting Update button The very first update routine may take a while, but subsequent update requests will be faster. Right after hitting Save to Geometry Cache button CLO and Marvelous Designer will be unresponsive for a while, and there will be a pop-up window in the CLO/MD LiveSync Editor once CLO and Marvelous Designer finishes sending animation data to Unreal. Try not to press the button multiple times in a row, otherwise unexpected crashes may happen. As garment data is detailed and can be heavy, putting in multiple garment assets (Static Mesh, Skeletal Mesh, or Geometry Cache) in a world may result in reduced performance in terms of FPS. For Static Mesh, Nanite can be a great choice and it is compatible with Static Mesh version of imported garment. Details about Nanite can be found in the following link: Nanite Virtualized Geometry Our default way of expressing transparent garment is dithered opacity (see a reference YouTube video). This method may result in fine noises on mesh surfaces due to its characteristics. If Order Independent Translucency option is enabled, it is possible to make meshes without the surface noises by altering a property of a desired material. Open up a desired material, and change its Blend Mode to Translucent. Occasionally LiveSync usage may yield the following error regarding lack of memory, which leads to a crash issue. In this case, if you separate an avatar and garment into more than 2 ZPRJ files from a single ZPRJ file, sending the avatar and garment separately may resolve the crash issue temporarily.

Title: [Experimental] Expressing Fur in Unreal Engine via LiveSync
Content: This feature is available from CLO LiveSync 1.1.0. Note that this is only available in CLO at the moment, and it will be supported in Marvelous Designer as render only fabrics are implemented in Marvelous Designer. This feature may result in unexpected crashes due to high memory usage of displaying Fur in Unreal Engine. Saving garments with Fur as Static Mesh First, assign Fur to desired Fabric(s), and apply the Fabric(s) to your garment. Then simply use Update feature to seamlessly bring garments to LiveSync Editor. The results can be saved as Static Mesh, and it can be observed that a Groom Asset is generated along with a Static Mesh. Locate a Static Mesh asset in Outliner, and click on it to add a child component by clicking the Add button and selecting Groom Component. Once a Groom Component is added as a child component of a Static Mesh for your garments, a correct Groom Asset can be assigned to it. You can either drag a desired Groom Asset from Content Browser, or search for it by clicking on Groom Asset section in Details panel. For more information on how to edit your Groom Asset, you can check out the official Groom Asset Editor User Guide on Epic Developer Community. Saving animated garments with Fur as Geometry Cache The setup for Geometry Cache is almost identical, and it only requires one additional step. For Geometry Cache, an additional Groom Binding asset is created. In a desired Geometry Cache asset, add a Groom Component as a child component, and assign a Groom Asset and a Groom Binding Asset to it. Keep in mind that this feature is experimental, and a Geometry Cache asset containing Fur information may result in a crash issue. Applying Simulation to Imported Fur Physics simulation can be applied on Groom Assets. For more information, please take a look at the official guide for Enabling Physics Simulation on Grooms. Note that enabling physics simulation can result in reduced performance or unexpected crash issues.

Title: Using LiveSync via CLO/MD LiveSync Editor
Content: There are 2 major features in the toolbar of CLO/MD LiveSync Editor, Update and Save: Update: The update button (CLO Virtual Fashion logo) allows users to instantly bring garment and avatar into CLO/MD LiveSync Editor. Note that you can delete loaded garment and/or avatar by selecting Garment and/or Avatar in a selection tree in the left side of the editor screen, then hitting a Delete key. Make sure that simulation and animation has been turned off in CLO and Marvelous Designer, and set in either Simulation mode or UV Editor mode when attempting to press Update button. In order to utilize Unified Material option embedded in ellipsis next to Update button, make sure that UV maps are arranged without overlapping with each other. UV maps can be manually arranged, or automatically arranged with Auto UV Packing/UV Packing. Texture resolution is supported up to 8K. Unified Material option can be particularly useful when Puckering is applied to garment, or multiple Trim objects are present. Otherwise, the option can be turned off. Incorrect UV mapping for Unified Material: maps are placed on texture boundary lines An example of maps being placed correctly, using UV Packing feature Save: Once garment and avatar are sent to CLO/MD LiveSync Editor, they can be saved as Static Mesh, Skeletal Mesh, Geometry Cache or Animation Sequence depending on users' needs. After selecting a desired asset in LiveSync tree, it can be saved as one of four aforementioned Unreal Engine assets. Pressing Save button automatically disables target asset options that CLO/MD LiveSync Editor cannot save based on source data in CLO and Marvelous Designer (e.g. no animation in CLO or Marvelous Designer means that assets cannot be saved as Geometry Cache). GC Material Combiner (new feature in LiveSync 1.1.5): GC Material Combiner can be launched by navigating to LiveSync Editor &gt Tools &gt GCMaterialCombiner. This tool aims to help users with managing materials of multiple Geometry Cache assets. Base Geometry Cache slot takes a single Geometry Cache asset which will be used as a reference. Multiple Geometry Cache assets can be added under Target Geometry Caches slot. As long as the number of material slots for given Geometry Cache assets is same, material of Base Geometry Cache will be applied to all Geometry Cache assets listed in Target Geometry Caches. You can choose to delete 'unused/duplicate' materials by enabling Delete all Other Materials checkbox. Then materials for Target Geometry Caches will be deleted accordingly.
ContentDescription: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide to the key features of the CLO/MD LiveSync Editor toolbar, including the Update and Save functions, along with instructions for utilizing the Unified Material option and the new GC Material Combiner tool.

Title: Opening CLO/MD LiveSync Editor
Content: Navigate to CLO/MD Live Sync Editor by going to Window &gt CLO/MD LiveSync Editor. When opening Live Sync Editor for the first time, you may get a warning pop-up window saying Missing Project Settings. Simply click Enable Missing, then click Restart Now in the second pop-up window. Then your Unreal Project will restart, and LiveSync becomes ready to be used. We highly recommend you to create a new Unreal project when starting with LiveSync, as LiveSync requires a couple of experimental features to be enabled, which may conflict with assets if LiveSync is added to existing projects. Note that asset migration can be utilized to bring assets from another project into a new project. Unreal Engine features and assets requiring DirectX 12 is not fully compatible with LiveSync at the moment.
ContentDescription: This web page provides essential steps and recommendations for successfully setting up and using the CLO/MD Live Sync Editor in Unreal Engine, ensuring a smooth integration with your projects.

Title: Frequently asked questions
Content: Q: Can I use LiveSync with multiple instances of CLO or Marvelous Designer, or multiple Unreal Engine instances? A: Unfortunately LiveSync is designed to work with a single instance of CLO or Marvelous Designer along with one Unreal Editor. Q: When I send garments to Unreal Engine, the looks are different. Is it possible to make them look same? A: Due to inherent differences in rendering systems, 'similar' looks are achieved, but it is nearly impossible to achieve identical looks. If you use CLO's V-Ray renderer, you can use UE5's Path Tracer as both utilize raytracing. Q: Which texture maps are sent to Unreal Engine via LiveSync? A: The following texture maps are gathered and sent to Unreal Engine: Base color map Normal map Roughness map Metallic map Reflection map Opacity map
ContentDescription: This webpage provides essential information about the functionality and limitations of LiveSync between CLO, Marvelous Designer, and Unreal Engine, including compatibility, visual consistency, and texture map transmission.

Title: What is LiveSync?
Content: LiveSync is a bridge which connects CLO and Unreal Editor (CLO LiveSync), or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Editor (MD LiveSync), and aims to shorten workflows requiring rendering in Unreal Engine. This is particularly useful if your workflow involves CLO or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, however, it is worth noting that intermediate process of using other software products may be eventually eliminated as LiveSync continues to get updated. Traditional workflows involve repetitive yet tedious and destructive process of exporting garments as desired file formats and importing the results in Unreal Engine, since users need to manually manage properties expressing realistic garments in CLO or Marvelous Designer. This is caused by limitations of using specific file formats, and you can only imagine fatigue accumulated from doing file exports, imports, and potentially redoing everything if design for garments needs to be adjusted in CLO or Marvelous Designer. By establishing a direct bridge, CLO and Marvelous Designer can communicate with Unreal Editor, eliminating needs for file exports and imports. LiveSync features and workflows can be found in Using LiveSync via CLO/MD LiveSync Editor and MetaHuman workflow with LiveSync. LiveSync Tutorial

Content: Objective Create Scene&ampProp items by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Required &amp Recommended Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling a Prop. [Required] "Prop" refers to any prop mesh that goes into the Scene/Stage. The file should not include anything other than Prop meshes. (e.g. Select Prop Mesh only when exporting) The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. In the Description, the following information about the product must be provided. (1) UV MAP unwrapping status O or X [Recommended] It is recommended to apply the same material to the part using the same material. UVs should be unwrapped so that they do not overlap so that customers can use a variety of textures. If mesh and the normal map have the same location and direction, it may cause overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Be careful not to overlap the mesh. If the two vertices are overlapping, please weld them together. For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. (e.g., logo and pattern) It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 2048 pixels. The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. It is recommended to add a wire to express the sharp edge. Details 1. Converting ZSE format in CLO software: Only CLO-formatted files can be uploaded to CONNECT. In Scene&ampProp, the term 'Prop' refers to backgrounds and props, while 'Scene' encompasses the whole setup, including Props, Light settings, and Custom Views. All props are saved as ZSE format in CLO software. To save as ZSE format, you need to have OBJ files. If you have a different format other than OBJ, export as an OBJ format file from other 3D MODELING software. 1-1. Open CLO 1-2. Import OBJ as Scene&ampProp TYPE From the main menu, click FILE IMPORT OBJ Select a file and click OPEN Object Type Scene&ampProp Scale After setting the value as when you work with different tools, then click OK 2. How to modify Scene&ampProp format 2-1. Modify the materials of Prop Select the IMPORTED PROP file, and then you can change the material and properties of PROP in the Property Editor. In the Material(Selected) section, you can load a texture or choose the material of TRIM (e.g., Metal, Plastic, Gem) 2-2. Rotate PROP so that it can be well-seen from the front. If you press the number 2 on the keyboard in CLO, you can see the front view. When viewed from the front, if the PROP is lying down, rotate it so you can see it well. Note : To easily rotate the PROP, right-click in the 3D viewer background Gizmo Select Local Coordinate. Press the number 4 or 6 on the keyboard to see the front side, click PROP and hold down the SHIFT and rotate vertically. 3. Save as Scene&ampProp When saving in Scene&ampProp format, the file name should be written the same as the product name registered on CONNECT. Ensuring the Prop is clearly visible from the front view in CLO and then saving it will guarantee good visibility in the viewer when the file is uploaded later. From the main menu, click FILE SAVE AS Scene&ampProp Select Auto or Custom thumbnail when saving. Select the location to save, and enter the product name to sell, and click SAVE. When saving in Scene&ampProp format, note that the set Light, Render, Custom View settings are also saved along with the file. 4. Title: Creating Pose
Content: Objective Create a Pose file (.pos) by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. 1. How to Create a pose file (.pos) 1-1. Creating a Pose file (.pos) using an avatar file (.avt). 1-2. Creating a Pose File (.pos) using FBX, GLB, or GLTF. 1-1. Creating a Pose file (.pos) using an avatar file (.avt) To create a pose file (.pos) by manipulating the joints of an avatar (.avt), you must have an avatar file with joints already set up. 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on File &gt Open &gt Avatar, or click on Avatar &gt Open in the Library. 3. In the 3D Window, go to Avatar Display &gt Show Avatar Joint (Shift + X) to switch to the avatar's joint mode. 4. Move the Avatar's joints to create your desired poses. 5. From the main menu, click on File &gt Save as &gt Pose. 6. After entering the name and path for a pose file (.pos), save it. Note: Pose files (.pos) generated with CLO or Marvelous Designer's official Avatars (FV2, MV2, KV1) are fully compatible with each other. 1-2. Creating a Pose file (.pos) using FBX, GLB, or GLTF. Create a pose file (.pos) using FBX, GLB, or GLTF files with Pre-defined pose settings. FBX, GLB, or GLTF file MUST contain the Avatar Mesh and Joints, with identical names and joint structures to the avatar file (.avt) that the pose file (.pos) will be applied. 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on File &gt Import &gt FBX / GLB / GLTF. 3. Select and open the FBX, GLB, or GLTF file you want to utilize for the Pose file (.pos). 4. Manipulate the Avatar's Joint to create the desired pose. 5. From the main menu, click on File &gt Save As &gt Pose. 6. After entering the name and path for a pose file (.pos), save it. Note: The pose file (.pos) will not work properly if you are applying it to an avatar with a different joint structure. 2. NORMAL MAP, DISPLACEMENT MAP, OPACITY MAP, ROUGHNESS MAP, METALNESS MAP, BASE MAP (FUR) 1-2. If you are going to sell the actual products, enter the URL of the sales page. Title: Creating Hair
Content: Objective Create ZACS content by using CLO software. (The 'Register Accessory' function, which registers accessory files (*.zacs), is only available in CLO and is not supported in Marvelous Designer.) 1. How to Create Hair to be registered as Accessory (ZACS) 1-1. Create Hair in other 3D software. 1-2. Create Hair with the patterns in CLO. 1-1. Create Hair in other 3D software. Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling Hair. Required &amp Recommended [Required] The accessory file must be created in FBX / OBJ / COLLADA format to be registered as the ZACS. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. The file should not include anything other than Hair meshes. (e.g. select Hair Mesh only when exporting) Please specify the compatible avatars for the ZACS in the Description. [Recommended] It is strongly recommended to create hair mesh using a maximum of 200,000 triangles, and please make sure that the polygon count does not go over 200,000. If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. It is recommended to use textures using a maximum of 2048 pixels. It is recommended to create hair that does not exceed the shoulder line. (For long hair, it is essential to 'Deactivate Avatar.') Create a thumbnail image that shows the item well, which is recommended to be 400*300 pixels. To avoid abnormal collisions between garments and hair during simulation, creating a transparent Dummy Mesh that covers the entire hair is recommended. (Please refer to the Dummy Mesh Guide) Modifying content provided by other platforms may violate copyrights and result in the removal of the item. Before proceeding with hair production, you must prepare the avatar file for generating accessories (ZACS). If you already prepared an avatar to utilize for accessories (ZACS), you can skip this step. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. Export the avatar as OBJ / FBX / GLTF or any format suitable for your 3D program. 4. Import the avatar file saved in step #3 into your 3D program and create a Hair Mesh. 5. Save the created Hair Mesh as FBX / OBJ / COLLADA. 1-2. Create Hair with the patterns in CLO. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. Create hair with the patterns in CLO. 2. Registering ZACS Register either hair mesh created in other 3D programs or hair with patterns as the ZACS. 1. Run CLO 2. Import the Avatar File into CLO. From the main menu, File &gt Open &gt Avatar &gt Register ACCESSORY &gt Select the Avatar file (AVT) that you want to utilize for ACCESSORY. 3. From the main menu, Avatar &gt Register Accessory Basic Accessory Type : Hair Object [File/Pattern] File Click the Folder icon to load the 3D file to be registered as Accessory. Scale : Adjust the scale of the Hair. Axis Conversion : Adjust the axis of the Hair. Pattern Select the patterns that you wish to register as Accessory (ZACS). However, the pattern to be converted must be created in advance before registering as an accessory. Note: After selecting the patterns to be converted into an accessory, you can register them as an accessory by right-clicking on the pattern in the 3D window, and then selecting Convert &gt to Avatar Accessory. Option Thumbnail [Auto/Custom] : Register the Thumbnail image for the ZACS to be created. When 'Auto' is selected, the Thumbnail image will be generated automatically. When 'Custom' is selected, click the '+' button to select the Thumbnail image you want to register. Save After choosing the save path for the ZACS, click the Save (S) button to generate the ZACS. 3. Modifying the material of ZACS You can modify the textures and materials applied to the generated ZACS in Property Editor. 1. Click on the ZACS in the 3D window. 2. Apply textures and materials in the Property Editor. 4. Saving the ZACS Save the Hair ZACS file with all textures and materials applied. 1. from the main menu, File &gt Save As &gt Accessory 2. After specifying the file name and directory path, click Save (S). 3. Save Accessory Select Accessory : Select the type of Accessories (ZACS) Use Custom Image : Register Thumbnail image. Note: If you want to utilize the Thumbnail image that was created when registering the ZACS as is, you can leave it unchecked. 4. Click 'OK.' 5. TITLE (Mandatory) Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. 3. Title: Creating 3D Garment
Content: Objective Create Garment content using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Required &amp Recommended When creating and uploading a Garment file, please follow the rules below. [Required] The garment file format must be *zprj, *zpac. The garment should be simulated on your avatar (including hangers). The garment file may include an official CLO/Marvelous Designer avatar or an avatar with an authorized resale license when you upload an item in the Garment Category. The sewing lines should not be twisted. Collision issues between layers should be resolved if you are designing a layered garment. It is not possible to delete/add/replace the Trim and Fabric files after Publish. It is not possible to add, delete, or replace different Design Sources after Publish, for garments that include Design Sources. The majority of the components should consist of 2D patterns produced by pattern-making in CLO or Marvelous Designer software. The 2D pattern should have a reasonable particle distance. The recommended particle distance value is 5 to 20. 2D patterns should be arranged as neatly as possible in the center. Avoid overlapping patterns in the 2D Pattern window. 2D patterns that are the same pieces(e.g. Jackets, Pants, etc.) should be close to each other and should be easily recognized as one piece. The unnecessary notches and baselines inside the 2D pattern should be deleted before publishing. [Recommended] The garment should have Fitting Suit information for compatibility with the Auto Fitting function. The garment should be saved after deactivating the Strengthen, Freeze feature. You have to save the garment after simulating it in the A pose or the T pose. A collision between trims should be resolved if trim category items (e.g., Buttons, Zippers, Hardware, Fasteners, Notions) are added to the garment. Details 1. Loading Avatar - Use the default avatar from the software. Library Avatar - Use a customized Avatar from the software. Main Menu File Open Avatar Fitting Suit - CLO Software Users CLO's default avatar is wearing a Fitting Suit. Fitting Suit is a device that helps the CLO's Auto Grading function to work. If both avatars have Fitting Suit information when wearing the same 3D costume to different size avatars, they can be draped to the appropriate size for each avatar without any special pattern modification. If the outfit uploaded by the Seller is a ZPAC file using the CLO default avatar, the Auto Grading feature makes it easier for buyers to use 3D costumes. - Marvelous Designer Software Users The Marvelous Designer default avatar is also wearing a Fitting Suit. You can also add Fitting Suit information to your avatar if you are using the Marvelous Designer software version 10 or higher. Please refer to the link for detailed instructions. 2. Creating Patterns / Sewing / Simulation Create patterns using the pattern generation tool from the 2D window. Sew patterns created by using the sewing tool from the 3D or 2D window. When sewing is completed, press the simulation button to simulate the costume on the avatar. Particle distance For smooth operation speed, we recommend working at the default value of 20. When submitting the final costume file, make sure that the particle spacing is set as a reasonable value. By default, 5 is recommended, and 3 is recommended if the pattern is small. Layer When creating a costume with multiple layers, it must collide between layers. You can set the order of layers by setting the layer value from the simulation properties pane. It is recommended to change the value to zero after the simulation is complete. 3. Setting up textures From the Properties Editor, you can add/modify textures that are used for garments. 4. Saving Files Save the garment file according to the specified file format. - ZPAC Main Menu File Save as Garment If you save it through the above path, the only garment except the avatar is automatically saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as ZPAC. - ZPRJ Main Menu File Save as Project If you save it through the above path, the garment including the avatar is saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as .zprj. Note: Only ZPAC or ZPRJ files can be uploaded in the Garment category. 5. Creating Render Image Allows all 3D Window screenshots or images rendered by other software. 6. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description When uploading the GARMENT to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers. If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process. 1. TITLE (Mandatory) Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. 3. Content: Objective The portfolio is a page where you can introduce yourself and organize your items. Details 1. Register CREATOR Information ① BANNER IMAGE Register the image from the banner.
